title.narrative: Strengthening the commitment of civil society organisations to human rights and democracy in Afar and Tigray, Ethiopia

description.narrative: Direct target groups: Civil Society Organizations (CSO): a total of 50 CSOs, 20 from Samara, Afar region and 30 from Mekelle, Tigray region — working in the areas of human rights, democracy, peace-buildingpeacebuilding, development, and community-based engagements will directly participate in this project. The project aims to strengthen and empower these CSOs, amplifying community voices and addressing related human rights concerns at both the regional and federal levels in a collective manner. The 50 CSOs (100 representatives) will form a network or coalition to advocate for the protection of human rights and democracy in these areas. Representatives of regional state institutions: A total of 86 representatives from the Afar and Tigray regional State Councils, Justice, and Law Enforcement organs receive training in the areas of HRBA to law making, and the role of CSOs in complementing the public outreach on draft/approved laws, civic education, and awareness on the role of the state councils. They will also be connected through inter-institutional, inter-regional and CSO-state institution forums jointly discussto jointly discuss and address human-rights related policy questions and foster better dialogue and understanding between the different actors. Indirect target groups: According to the World Population review (2024), the estimated population of the two intervention regions (Afar and Tigray) is approximately 8,000,000. CEHRO anticipates that 40% of this population will be reached through community awareness-raising efforts, CSO multipliers, dialogue events, and media campaigns. Intermediaries, including journalists/local media houses, academic institutions, CBOs, FBOs, and human rights and democratic institutions such as the EHRC and NEBE regional branches, will be indirectly targeted and will be called upon to act as allies in raising awareness on human rights and democracy issues. A total of 80 individuals will be involved.

Impact: The respect for human rights within state institutions is enhanced through effective human rights monitoring and advocacy by civil society organizations (CSOs) at the Afar and Tigray regions levels Outcome: 50 civil society organizations (CSOs) and 86 representatives of state institutions in the Afar and Tigray regions are making use of their strengthened capacities in human rights-based approaches, participatory policy decision-making, effective collaboration, and inclusive accountability.

The project aims to improve respect for human rights by state institutions in the Afar and Tigray regions through effective monitoring and advocacy by civil society organizations (CSOs). To this end, the Ethiopian partner organization CEHRO (Consortium of Ethiopian Human Rights Organizations) will work with local CSOs to establish communities of practice in which CSOs can network and develop joint strategies. At the same time, exchange forums will be organized between regional institutions (regional parliaments as well as judicial and law enforcement authorities) to ensure a sustainable and coordinated implementation of the human rights-based approach. Finally, regular exchanges between CSOs and state representatives will be organized.
